comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C36-C37 regarding temporal characteristics. Both evaluations support that ketamine effects are acute without carryover, though peer reviewers question the relationship to sustained antidepressant effects.

Both address claims C60-C62 about methodological contributions. OpenEval finds the approach fully supported, while peer reviewers express uncertainty about broader implications, with Reviewer 2 questioning whether findings are more relevant to reinforcement learning than depression research.

Strong agreement on claims C25-C27, C31-C32 regarding dissociation between behavioral effects and oculomotor side effects. Both evaluations support this finding, though peer reviewers question broader interpretations about antidepressant mechanisms.

Agreement on claims C28, C82 regarding negative findings. Both evaluations support that ketamine did not affect motivation, memory, or temporal credit assignment, accepting these as valid null results that characterize ketamine's selectivity.
Agreement on claims C21-C24 regarding oculomotor side effects. Both evaluations support the nystagmus findings with appropriate statistical support, accepting these as documented side effects.

Divergence on claims C18-C19, C41-C42, C81 regarding model selection and generalizability. OpenEval finds the best-fitting ketamine model supported across subjects, while Reviewer 2 raises concerns about parameter-specificity and generalizability due to different models fitting different subjects.

Both address main findings (C29-C30, C59) about ketamine's selective effect on loss processing. OpenEval finds these summary claims supported by convergent evidence, and peer reviewers explicitly affirm the core finding with the editor calling evidence 'solid.'
Agreement on claims C12-C13, C69 regarding pharmacokinetic validation. Both evaluations support the dose comparisons and drug exposure data as methodologically sound without challenge.

Partial overlap on background claims C33-C35. OpenEval finds these appropriately cited, while peer reviewers (particularly Reviewer 1) express concern about framing regarding antidepressant mechanisms and depression pathophysiology in the introduction.

Both address claim C56 about affective memory resistance. OpenEval rates as uncertain/speculative, and peer reviewers similarly question the connection to antidepressant effects, noting weak or incomplete evidence for this interpretation.

Both address claim C55 about mechanisms linking acute to long-term effects. OpenEval rates as uncertain/speculative, and peer reviewers express similar concerns, with Reviewer 2 stating authors provide 'little to no support for this link.'

OpenEval evaluates claims C6-C9, C47-C76 regarding experimental design and baseline behavioral findings as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these methodological and baseline characterization claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims C16-C17, C77-C78 regarding model selection and BIC comparison for baseline models as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these baseline model selection claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims C43-C44 comparing findings to prior work and interpreting selective effects on outcome evaluation as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these comparative interpretations.
